goal.summary: MPI-475's judgement run PASSED on the correct transformer and the model's whole claim holds. MPI-476's items 1/3/4 confirmed in Electron; item 2 did NOT pass - it exposed a wrong VRAM floor on three shipped cards and a RAM column that showed the same figure for two different cards, both now fixed and both needing a re-check. A long bench investigation into a hi-res fix produced a NEGATIVE result worth more than the feature would have been: H3's DiT does not accept an upscaled latent, proven by elimination. A 2k tier shipped on measured evidence instead. MPI-477 carries the one route left.

VRAM floor fixed at the ladder, not per card (5e0a6a2a). Wan read '16GB minimum' because the computed floor was rounded onto the 8GB grid, which has NO 12 in it. Three cards were wrong: wan-22 (8.29 fit), ltx-23-balanced (10.10), qwen-edit (8.02), all catapulted to 16. Floors now lift onto CARD_SIZES (8/12/16/then 8s). Every 8GB-floor model's table is byte-identical.

RAM column now rounds to 4GB, not 8 (b677eeeb). Wan showed '12GB -> 24GB' and '16GB -> 24GB', the same figure twice, which tells a user a 16GB card buys nothing. It buys 4GB. Still ceil, so still only over-states. Side effect: the LTX calibration anchor now comes out EXACT (44GB at 16GB VRAM, the measured 4060 Ti figure) instead of rounded to 48. 17 of 20 models moved; verified monotonic.

MpiLatentUpscale written, committed in ComfyUi-MpiNodes (8482649). Core CANNOT upscale an H3 latent at all - LatentUpscaleBy dies with "'NestedTensor' object has no attribute 'reshape'" - and core additionally converts pixels with a hardcoded // 8. This node unbinds the pair, scales only the half with spatial dims (picked by dim() >= 5), passes the audio half through, re-nests, and takes its target in PIXELS with a stride input.

THE HI-RES FIX IS DISPROVEN ON H3, by elimination rather than argument. Every latent UPSCALE produced hard horizontal banding; the one DOWNSCALE did not; native 2560x1472 is clean. Eliminated in turn: the interpolation method (nearest-exact AND bicubic), the scale ratio (x1.5 uniform AND x1.9), and output vs denoised_output. Conclusion: the DiT does not accept an upscaled latent.

2k tier added to H3 (6dd921a3) - the SAME numbers LTX already ships (1472/2560), earned by a measured clean 2560x1472 run. UI needed nothing: MpiOptionSelector already maps '2k' with a 'detail-focused, low motion' hint. ratios.js used to say 'do not add a 2K/4K tier', which conflated a 2K CANVAS with the API-only H3-Regenerate-2K SECOND PASS; the comment now separates them. Still no 4k tier.

key_decisions: The hi-res fix was pursued to a NEGATIVE result and that is the session's most valuable output. H3's DiT does not accept an upscaled latent: every upscale banded, the one downscale did not, native is clean. Interpolator, ratio, and output-vs-denoised_output were each eliminated by test. Do not let a future session re-run this - MPI-477's brief leads with the table.

ref2va composes for the stage-1 canvas, and it is STRUCTURAL: MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo sets minimax_refs and never minimax_keyframes, so nothing anchors the framing. The same prompt and seed framed a close shot on the dragon's head at 672x384 and staged the whole scene at 1344x768. Any technique that samples the first pass small changes the SHOT, not just its resolution. Expect the technique to behave far better on fl2va i2v.

The audio breaks on a SPLIT trajectory, not on a refiner. H3 emits video and audio from ONE joint latent and the audio half is bound to the video half's token layout. A split-sigma hi-res fix cuts the trajectory in half and the audio never completes; a full pass plus a separate denoise<1 pass leaves pass 1's audio intact. The two techniques were being conflated and ref2va.md now separates them in a table.

MpiNodes stride stays 16. It was changed to 32 on the user's inference (VAE 16 x DiT patch 2) and committed, then reverted (43a976f) when the measurement landed: a 2016x1152 request decoded at 1008x576, exactly half, which proves the decode multiplies by 16.

The VRAM floor was fixed on the LADDER rather than by hanging minVramGb on three cards. minVramGb survives for what it is actually for - a model measured to run below the fit, as both H3 cards are at 12 against a 13.3 fit.

Wan 2.2, LTX 2.3 Balanced and Qwen Image Edit each said 16GB of VRAM where 12 is enough (the minimum was rounded onto a grid of 8s, which has no 12 in it - the most common mid-range card size), and the RAM column rounded the same way, so it could print the same figure for two different cards. Should ref_image_size default flip from `match` to `max`? The user reports max usually gives the better result, at ~14 vs 11-12 s/step with one reference. Arguably the default should ship the good result and let people trade down for speed. Recorded in ref2va.md as an open question, not decided.

Do reference tokens dominate per-step cost on ref2va? Two of the session's own timings suggest yes (1152x640 2s 10 steps = 518s vs 2560x1472 1s 10 steps = 544s - about 2.4x the pixel-frames for the same wall time). If they do, every canvas-reduction technique saves far less than the fl2va pixel curve predicts, which decides whether MPI-477 is worth opening at all. Two cheap runs settle it: same canvas, once with references and once bare.
